description: A next-generation planetary exploration framework. Our system combines autonomous Phobos resource analysis with advanced Mars surface mapping capabilities, driven by robust propulsion, thermal power units, and a mobile rover designed for multi-stage space missions.
summary:
MARS TO PHOBOS: Mapping the Path

Our project presents an integrated concept for Martian exploration, focusing on surface mapping of the southern polar region. By considering topographic, optical, thermal, and geological data from NASA missions, we aim to identify potential landing areas, terrain hazards, scientific locations, and suitable rover routes.

Beyond mapping, we propose a robotic Mars–Phobos exploration architecture. A Martian lander investigates local resources, while a separate rover studies the surface and regolith of Phobos. The mission concept also explores collecting Martian CO₂ and converting it into carbon monoxide through electrolysis, potentially providing propellant for a conceptual electric propulsion system.

Solar concentrators and a Stirling engine are considered as a possible power source, supported by energy storage and thermal management systems.

Our goal is to connect planetary mapping, robotic exploration, and in-situ resource utilization, demonstrating how NASA data can support safer exploration and help prepare for future human missions.
details: Teamwork and Development Process The project was primarily developed through independent concept design and collaborative research. As team captain, I was responsible for the original mission architecture, technical concepts, and overall design direction. I developed ideas from earlier mission plans and expanded them into a broader Mars–Phobos exploration concept. I also investigated different engineering approaches, including electric propulsion, plasma and ion propulsion concepts, power generation, thermal management, and resource utilization. During development, I used AI as a technical discussion and verification tool. It helped me examine the theoretical and practical feasibility of my ideas, identify possible limitations, compare alternative approaches, and explore suggestions such as Peltier-based thermal management. AI also supported the preparation and organization of the presentation materials. The final design decisions and selection of concepts remained my responsibility. Hso, aras1907, rumball11, and agamzey contributed mainly to the communication and presentation stage. They helped organize the technical ideas into slides, prepared visual materials, and assisted with the English demonstration and detailed presentation. AI-assisted translation was also used in preparing the presentation. Our workflow separated the technical development of the concept from its visual communication, allowing the team to turn an individual engineering concept into a structured project presentation.
